transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… so, I came in because at work it’s starting to become a real problem that I can’t seem to stay where I’m supposed to stay. Like, I’m a production worker, and I’ll be at my station, and then I just kind of… pop up or walk off before I even really think about it. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult or ignore anyone, I just move, and then afterward I realize, okay, I was supposed to stay put.

And it’s not just on the floor. In meetings too, when everybody’s sitting or standing where they’re supposed to, I’ll get up or start moving around, and people notice. My supervisor has talked to me about it because they said it’s becoming a safety issue, like if I leave my station suddenly or take off at the wrong time, it can mess things up or put someone at risk. That scared me, honestly, because I don’t want to cause an accident or get fired, but it feels like my body reacts before my brain catches up.
Do you find yourself moving or getting up suddenly in other places, like at home or when you're out with friends or family, or does it only seem to happen at work?

It’s mostly what I’ve noticed at work, because that’s where it gets me in trouble, if that makes sense. Like at home, I might move around too, but nobody’s really telling me “stay in this exact spot,” so it doesn’t stand out the same way. At work, though, it’s really obvious because I’m supposed to stay at my station, or in a meeting I’m supposed to stay seated or stay where everyone else is, and I just… pop up.

It’s like I’ll be at my station and suddenly I’m walking off or shifting around before I even really decide to. Then a second later I’m like, wait, I wasn’t supposed to leave. And in meetings, same thing, I’ll get up or start moving when everyone else is still, and people notice. My supervisor has said it’s becoming a safety problem because if I leave my station like that, it can mess things up. That’s the part that made me come in, honestly, because I’m not trying to be careless, but my body kind of takes off before my brain catches it.
When you're at home or in other relaxed settings where you aren't required to stay in one place, do you still feel a need to move around or find it hard to sit still?

Yeah, I do. It’s just… it’s easier to ignore at home because there isn’t a rule I’m breaking, you know? But if I actually try to sit still or stand still, I feel it. Like this pressure starts building up in my body, kind of like I’m holding something in, and then I need to move.

At work it’s really obvious when I’m standing by the machine, because I’ll try to stay planted there and it feels almost uncomfortable, like I have to pace a little, or stretch, or go do something right then. And in training too, when I’m supposed to sit through it, I’ll be sitting there but my body is just like, no, move. It’s not even that I’m thinking, “I’m bored, I’m going to leave.” It feels more physical than that, like I need to get up or shift around before I can even calm down.
Have you ever experienced sudden, quick movements that you couldn’t control, like blinking your eyes, shrugging your shoulders, or jerking your head, even when you didn’t intend to do so?

Um… not that I’ve really noticed, no. I mean, I move a lot, but it doesn’t feel like a sudden twitch or something like my eye blinking over and over or my head jerking. It’s more like I get restless and then I’m up or shifting around, if that makes sense.

Like, I don’t think I have those quick little movements where I’m surprised by it or can’t stop a shrug or something. At least nobody’s pointed that out to me, and I haven’t caught myself doing it. I guess maybe everybody blinks or shifts sometimes, but nothing that stands out to me like what you’re describing.
Before you feel the need to move or shift around, do you ever get a warning feeling or a strong urge in your body that builds up until you have to move?

Yeah, I think so. It’s not like a twitch warning, exactly, but there’s definitely this feeling that builds up before I move. Like if I’m trying to stand still by the machine, I can feel this pressure in my body, almost like I’m holding myself in place and it gets harder and harder to keep doing it.

And then I start feeling like I have to do something right then — pace a little, stretch, shift my weight, walk over somewhere, anything. Same thing when I’m sitting through training. I’ll be sitting there trying to just stay put, but inside I’m getting more and more uncomfortable, like my body is saying, “Get up, move.” It builds until moving feels like the only way to make it settle down.
Have you ever had trouble with this restlessness or sudden movement in school, social situations, or other parts of your life that affected your performance or relationships?

Yeah… it’s definitely affected things, especially at work. That’s probably where it’s caused the most real problems, because it’s not just like, “Oh, I’m fidgety,” you know? It turns into me not staying where I’m supposed to be, or moving around when I should be focused on the machine or the handoff, and then people see it as me not taking it seriously.

I’ve been written up by supervisors for safety stuff and production problems, and that’s been really stressful because I’m trying to keep my job and move forward there. I’ve also been trying to work toward getting certified, and this kind of puts that at risk too, because if they don’t trust me to stay on task or be steady during the process, then it’s like… why would they sign off on me?

And with coworkers, it’s awkward. Some of them don’t really want to partner with me during handoffs now, or they act hesitant, like they’d rather work with someone else because they think I’m going to be all over the place or miss something. That part feels embarrassing, honestly, because I’m not trying to make anyone’s job harder. But it has affected how people see me at work.
Looking back at your childhood, did you have similar issues with restlessness or difficulty staying in one place, especially during school or structured activities?

Yeah, definitely. Looking back, it was there really early, like even in elementary school. I was kind of known as the kid who could not just sit in the chair and be quiet like everybody else seemed to do.

I remember getting in trouble for being out of my seat, like wandering around the room or going over to someone’s desk when I wasn’t supposed to. And I’d talk over the teacher a lot, not even always trying to be rude, just like the thought came out before I could stop it. I’d blurt answers or comments, or interrupt when the teacher was explaining something.

There were notes sent home about it too — like me not staying seated, talking too much, blurting things out, moving around the classroom. It wasn’t just once or twice. It was kind of a pattern. I think adults saw it as me being disruptive or not listening, but I remember feeling like sitting still was almost impossible sometimes, especially when we had to be quiet for a long time or do something structured.
Outside of work and school, do you also find it hard to stay still or feel restless in other structured situations like meetings, religious services, or public events?

Yeah, it’s not only work or school stuff. Any time I’m expected to just be still for a while, I start getting that same feeling in my body. Like if I’m sitting somewhere structured, I’ll try to stay put, but then it’s like this pressure starts building up inside me.

It’s hard to explain because it’s not pain, exactly. It’s more like my body feels trapped or wound up, and the longer I sit or stand there, the more I feel like I need to move right then. I’ll start shifting around, stretching, changing positions, or wanting to get up and walk somewhere even if there’s not really a reason to. If I’m standing still, I’ll keep moving my weight from one foot to the other or feel like I need to pace.

It’s like I can force myself for a little bit, but then it gets louder in my body, if that makes sense. Moving is what makes it calm down for a minute.
